references.text: Bezalel made the vessels for the table of showbread from pure gold: the plates, dishes, bowls, and cups for drink offerings, as described in Exodus 25:29.
Describes how the Levites were to cover the table of showbread with its plates, dishes, cups, and pitchers during transport.
The tribal leaders brought silver plates and bowls as offering gifts, similar to the gold utensils used for the table.
Solomon made bowls, knives, cups, plates, and fire pans from pure gold for the temple, corresponding to the utensils of the tabernacle.
Repeats that Solomon made utensils of pure gold for God's house, including bowls and cups.
Cyrus returned the gold and silver vessels that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem.
The prophecy that even the pots in Jerusalem shall be holy to the Lord, an eschatological extension of sacred vessels.
Theological contrast: Highlights the difference between the service at the bread table (gold/holy place) and the altar of sacrifice (bronze/sacrifice).
Continuity and confirmation: Confirms that the requirement for gold utensils for drink offerings remained valid even in later temple history.
Equipment and use: The source describes the making of vessels for pouring, while this verse describes the actual ritual action of the drink offering.
